owner_decisions.shell_parse_ruling: Don’t mark the security gate passed yet. Capture and pin the intended ruleset, then rerun against the unchanged candidate with rule identities and parse failures recorded. Supplementary scans must use those exact rules. For the unparsed shell sections, inspect the actual three rule definitions and document an equivalent targeted review of the complete affected files. Absence of a few literal strings and successful Bash parsing alone don’t establish security coverage. Keep the parser limitation explicit. If equivalent review substitutes for scanner coverage, record that as a change to the gate requiring my approval—not as a clean scan. No source rewrite or detection-rehearsal restart is needed merely to collect better evidence. The candidate can stay 24c0c00; any changes to covered scan tooling must follow the existing manifest policy.
owner_decisions.timeout: 1 — Supplementary full scan. A completed scan can close the coverage gap without changing the candidate. Record the candidate/file hash, scanner version, exact ruleset, command and clean result. Confirm the original scan’s only missing coverage was that file/rule combination. Keep the original timeout recorded as a failed attempt. The gate can pass on the combined coverage evidence, once finding triage is complete; don’t relabel the original scan as clean or waive the error. No source change or detection rerun is needed.
